Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Money, work & business

auction noun

also auctions, sell at auction, auctioneer, bid, bidding, public sale

classical

Plaut. Men. 1157: Auctiō fīet Menaechmī māne sānē septimī
Cic. Att. 13.14: auctiōnis diem (Lewis & Short)

auctiō, auctiōnis f.

noun, third declension

an auction

A sale to the highest bidder: a spear (hasta) was set up, a crier (praecō) called the bids and a banker took the money (Lewis & Short). To hold one, auctiōnem facere.

Other words

  • sub hastā vēndere — sell at auction

    verb phrase · also used · classical · Liv. 23.38.7: comitibusque eōrum sub hastā vēnditīs, and their companions sold at auction

  • liceor, licērī, licitus sum — bid (at an auction)

    also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.18.3: illō licente contrā licērī audeat nēmō, no one dares bid against him; Cic. Verr. 2.3.27: quī digitō sit licitus, who bid with a raised finger

    The goods themselves licent, fetch a price: vēnībunt quīquī licēbunt (Plaut. Men. 1159).

  • praecō, praecōnis m. — the crier who calls an auction; an auctioneer

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Hor. AP 419: ut praecō, ad mercēs turbam quī cōgit emendās, like a crier who gathers a crowd to buy the goods

Examples

  • Auctiō fīet Menaechmī māne sānē septimī. vēnībunt servī, supellex, fundī, aedēs, omnia. vēnībunt quīquī licēbunt, praesentī pecūniā.

    Menaechmus’s auction will be held bright and early on the seventh day. For sale: slaves, furniture, farms, house, everything. Sold at whatever they fetch, cash down.Plaut. Men. 1157–1159

See also sale, sell, price, buy.
